# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 38 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 38 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_038_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 8 — Abstain from Evil; Practice Good

**1** I said to him, "Sir, I now ask you to show me the powers of the evil spirits, that recognizing their deeds I may keep away from them." **2** He said to me: "Listen, then, to the works from which you must abstain. Abstain from evil-speaking, from adultery, from drunkenness, from wicked pleasure, from lawless eating, from pride and boastfulness, from lying and theft, and from all like things. **3** Do you think that these things are a small evil to a servant of God? A great evil is adultery and a great evil is drunkenness and a great evil is pride and boastfulness. These great evils are what servants of God must abstain from. **4** But hear also the works which you must practice: help the widow, visit the orphan and the poor man, redeem the servants of God from their distress, be hospitable to strangers, do not resist anyone, be humble, be more submissive than all men, honor the aged, practice righteousness, watch over brotherly love, endure injury, be long-suffering, do not bear a grudge, exhort those who are sick in soul, do not cast away those who have stumbled in faith, but convert them and give them courage; rebuke sinners, do not oppress debtors and the poor, and all the similar things. **5** Do you think these things are a small good to those who practice them? Not at all," he said. "They are exceedingly great! **6** I said to him, "Sir, I would like to know in which of these evil things I am involved, in order that I may turn from them." "Listen," he said. "I will tell you in which ones you are involved. Your business transactions and the many things which you have undertaken — let these not occupy you, but rather leave the business matters and cling to righteousness. **7** For if you do not abandon your business transactions with the many, you will not be able to observe the commandments of the Lord. And if you do not keep the commandments of the Lord, you will not be saved."

---

*EMET note: Mandate 8 is a two-column moral catalog: vices to avoid and virtues to practice. It is the most comprehensive ethical list in the Mandates. The closing personal application to Hermas (v.6-7) — business dealings distracting from righteousness — brings the mandate home to the specific audience.*
